text:
olivia_support: Customer rwd-corp reporting a sudden uptick in 429s and some intermittent 401s when they send long contexts (~8k tokens). Happening across both streaming and non-streaming calls. Anyone seen this combo before? :thinking:

ravi_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + payload) and say how many parallel connections they're opening? Also which model variant?

olivia_support: They use `rwd-large-v1` and run ~12 paral requests from a single host. Repro curl below (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"<~8000 token context>
Follow-up question...","max_tokens":512}'
```

olivia_support: Timeline: started ~2026-03-16T14:36Z, steady until ~14:42Z then 429 rate spiked to ~25% of calls. A few 401s interspersed.

chris_sre: Two likely signals: 1) per-model throughput hit (RPM/TPM) causing 429s 2) account billing state producing 401s for some auth checks. Are the 401s all for the same API key?

olivia_support: Yes same key. Customer says billing looked fine on their side. They saw a failed invoice yesterday but resolved it.

emma_billing: Checking our billing logs now — account did hit a failed payment event at 2026-03-15 23:05 UTC; system marked billing-action-required for a short window before auto-retry succeeded at 23:12 UTC. During that window, the account entered restricted state. That can produce 401s for some endpoints and reduced rate allowances until re-sync.

ratebot: automated: Billing state change detected for account rwd-corp: payment_failed -> pending -> settled. Auth errors may persist for up to 10 minutes while caches refresh.

ravi_eng: Ok — that explains 401s early on. For the 429s with long contexts: model serving enforces per-model token/min (TPM) and requests/min (RPM) soft-limits plus a max concurrent inflight requests cap. For `rwd-large-v1` we throttle at ~1200 RPM and ~200k TPM per model pool, with soft concurrency around 24 per pool. Hitting long contexts multiplies token consumption and can trip TPM quickly.

chris_sre: Also note our burst window: sustained short spikes (bursts) are allowed but when aggregate client-side concurrency + long ctx pushes token throughput above TPM, we start returning 429s rather than queueing indefinitely.

olivia_support: Customer was doing background prefetch of embeddings + generation chains (so extra tokens upstream). They also use client-side batched prefetcher that fires 6 requests at once every 100ms.

ravi_eng: Repro steps for engineering: please run the curl above with header `X-Request-ID: rwd-repro-2398` and reproduce with two modes: A) 12 parallel streams with full 8k context B) single stream sequential. Capture: HTTP status, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and our trace-id from response headers.

olivia_support: Got trace id from customer for a 429 response: trace-id=trc_20260316_9b3f. Also attached short server log snippet: 

```
[14:42:07] request=trc_20260316_9b3f status=429 model=rwd-large-v1 tokens_in_window=182340 tokens_this_request=8300 parallel_inflight=12
[14:42:07] action=throttle reason=tpm_exceeded window_seconds=60
```

chris_sre: That log line nails it — tokens_in_window ~182k ~= our TPM boundary. When tokens_this_request is huge it consumes a big slice of the window.

ravi_eng: Immediate mitigation guidance to give customer: 
- Reduce sent context length (trim to ~2k tokens) or send only incremental diffs.
- Limit parallelism to <6 while using long contexts.
- Stagger and jitter requests instead of tight bursts (randomized 200–800ms).
- Implement token-aware batching: send more smaller requests than fewer huge ones.
- If they need sustained high TPM, propose Dedicated capacity or request quota increase (prod review required).

olivia_support: Any suggestions on backoff strategy? They currently retry immediately a few times and get rapid 429s.

ravi_eng: Exponential backoff with jitter: initial 200ms, *2, cap 8s + full-jitter. Also respect Retry-After header when present. For streaming, consider reducing initial context and use prefix cache (we can enable KV-prefetching on server side for enterprise customers).

emma_billing: I'll confirm the billing cache flush timeline with infra. If the customer still sees auth failures, ask them to reissue a new API key after billing shows OK — that clears any lingering auth cache faster.

olivia_support: Action items: 1) Ask customer to run repro with X-Request-ID and send headers/traces 2) Recommend immediate mitigations (trim context, lower parallelism, backoff) 3) Offer Dedicated trial if they need sustained high token throughput 4) Emma to confirm billing cache TTL.

deploy-bot: note: staged fix pushed to rate-limiter config to extend soft-burst headroom by 10% for model pool rwd-large-v1 for next 15 min to help ongoing repros.

chris_sre: We'll follow up after repro. If they can share traces for both 401 and 429, we can correlate billing cache timing vs throttle windows.

olivia_support: Thanks all — I'll pass steps to customer and attach repro checklist. Will update thread when they respond. :white_check_mark:
